claim: AAV-mediated gene therapies are rapidly advancing to the clinic.
source: Adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated gene therapies are rapidly advancing to the clinic, and AAV engineering has resulted in vectors with increased ability to deliver therapeutic genes.
evidence: This is a general statement about the field supported by established knowledge in gene therapy research.

claim: AAV engineering has resulted in vectors with increased ability to deliver therapeutic genes.
source: Adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated gene therapies are rapidly advancing to the clinic, and AAV engineering has resulted in vectors with increased ability to deliver therapeutic genes.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in the field of AAV vector development.

claim: Quantitative comparison of AAVs, especially in large animals, remains challenging.
source: Although the choice of vector is critical, quantitative comparison of AAVs, especially in large animals, remains challenging.
evidence: This statement reflects the motivation for the study and is supported by inference from the need for the developed method.

claim: scAAVengr is an efficient single-cell AAV engineering pipeline to simultaneously quantify and rank efficiency of competing AAV vectors across all cell types in the same animal.
source: Here, we developed an efficient single-cell AAV engineering pipeline (scAAVengr) to simultaneously quantify and rank efficiency of competing AAV vectors across all cell types in the same animal.
evidence: This is the primary methodological claim of the paper, supported by the experimental data presented throughout.

claim: K912 was identified as a top performing variant using the scAAVengr workflow.
source: A top performing variant identified using this pipeline, K912, was used to deliver SaCas9 and edit the rhodopsin gene in macaque retina, resulting in editing efficiency similar to infection rates detected by the scAAVengr workflow.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the scAAVengr screening and validation experiments.

claim: K912 was used to deliver SaCas9 and edit the rhodopsin gene in macaque retina.
source: A top performing variant identified using this pipeline, K912, was used to deliver SaCas9 and edit the rhodopsin gene in macaque retina, resulting in editing efficiency similar to infection rates detected by the scAAVengr workflow.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing Cas9 expression and genome editing.

claim: K912-mediated editing efficiency was similar to infection rates detected by the scAAVengr workflow.
source: A top performing variant identified using this pipeline, K912, was used to deliver SaCas9 and edit the rhodopsin gene in macaque retina, resulting in editing efficiency similar to infection rates detected by the scAAVengr workflow.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of scAAVengr infection data with genome editing data.

claim: scAAVengr was used to identify top-performing AAV variants in mouse brain, heart, and liver following systemic injection.
source: scAAVengr was then used to identify top-performing AAV variants in mouse brain, heart, and liver following systemic injection.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mouse systemic injection experiments.

claim: A growing number of clinical trials are using AAV to treat diseases such as retinal degeneration, neurological disorders, and hemophilia.
source: A growing number of clinical trials are using AAV to treat diseases such as retinal degeneration, neurological disorders, and hemophilia, through gene replacement, genome editing, and optogenetics (High and Roncarolo, 2019; Sahel and Dalkara, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Gene therapies for Leber congenital amaurosis and spinal muscular atrophy have received FDA approval.
source: And, with the recent FDA approval for treatment of Leber congenital amaurosis and spinal muscular atrophy, gene therapies are rapidly becoming a clinical reality.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge of FDA approvals.

claim: Significant hurdles prevent the successful, widespread implementation of AAV-mediated gene therapies, including efficient gene delivery and immune response to viral vectors and gene products.
source: However, significant hurdles prevent the successful, widespread implementation of AAV-mediated gene therapies, including efficient gene delivery and immune response to viral vectors and gene products.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in the field of gene therapy.

claim: Recent efforts to reengineer viral vectors have shown promise for addressing issues with gene delivery and immune response.
source: Recent efforts to reengineer viral vectors have shown promise for addressing these issues, resulting in AAVs with improved abilities (Li and Samulski, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The selection of an optimal vector is essential to the success of gene therapy.
source: The selection of an optimal vector is essential to the success of the therapy.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in gene therapy development.

claim: Sufficient gene expression is critical for gene therapy success.
source: Sufficient gene expression is critical, while enhanced tropism and greater efficiency of gene delivery reduces the titer of vector required and decreases the likelihood of immune response.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in gene therapy.

claim: Enhanced tropism and greater efficiency of gene delivery reduces the titer of vector required and decreases the likelihood of immune response.
source: Sufficient gene expression is critical, while enhanced tropism and greater efficiency of gene delivery reduces the titer of vector required and decreases the likelihood of immune response.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge and logical inference in gene therapy.

claim: Quantitative comparisons of newly engineered vectors have in the past required large numbers of animals.
source: Quantitative comparisons of newly engineered vectors, including evaluation of transgene expression levels and cell-type tropism, have in the past required large numbers of animals, and therefore involved significant ethical and financial burden.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge of traditional AAV screening methods.

claim: In primates, large variability between animals due to differences in anatomy and immune responses has made comparisons between animals inaccurate.
source: Additionally, in primates, the large variability between animals, due to differences in anatomy and immune responses, has made comparisons between animals inaccurate.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge of primate research challenges.

claim: Primates are the most physiologically similar animal to humans.
source: In this work, the scAAVengr pipeline was applied to primates, which are the most physiologically similar animal to humans, and are thus a critical preclinical model.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in comparative biology.

claim: Successful clinical translation of gene therapies depends on highly efficient vectors for human tissue.
source: Successful clinical translation of gene therapies depends on highly efficient vectors for human tissue, and vector performance in small animals often does not accurately predict efficiency in primates.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in translational research.

claim: Vector performance in small animals often does not accurately predict efficiency in primates.
source: Successful clinical translation of gene therapies depends on highly efficient vectors for human tissue, and vector performance in small animals often does not accurately predict efficiency in primates.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in AAV vector development.

claim: Existing AAV vectors infect the primate retina significantly less efficiently than rodent retina.
source: For retinal gene therapy in particular, primates are essential, as existing AAV vectors infect the primate retina significantly less efficiently than in rodent retina (Dalkara et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Primates are the only animal model that has a macula and foveal pit.
source: Furthermore, primates are the only animal model that has a macula and foveal pit (the region of the retina responsible for high acuity vision in humans), making them the most relevant translational model.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in comparative anatomy.

claim: The pattern of AAV expression differs in foveal and peripheral retina.
source: Notably, the pattern of AAV expression also differs in foveal and in peripheral retina (Dalkara et al., 2013), with highest expression in the foveola and in a perifoveal ring of retinal ganglion cells, and punctate expression near blood vessels in the periphery.
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: AAV expression is highest in the foveola and in a perifoveal ring of retinal ganglion cells.
source: Notably, the pattern of AAV expression also differs in foveal and in peripheral retina (Dalkara et al., 2013), with highest expression in the foveola and in a perifoveal ring of retinal ganglion cells, and punctate expression near blood vessels in the periphery.
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: AAV expression is punctate near blood vessels in the peripheral retina.
source: Notably, the pattern of AAV expression also differs in foveal and in peripheral retina (Dalkara et al., 2013), with highest expression in the foveola and in a perifoveal ring of retinal ganglion cells, and punctate expression near blood vessels in the periphery.
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The scAAVengr pipeline can be applied to any species or tissue for which marker genes can be identified.
source: The scAAVengr pipeline can be applied to any species or tissue for which marker genes can be identified, however, as demonstrated here through screening performed in mouse brain, heart, and liver following systemic injections of pooled AAV library.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mouse tissues and inference about the method's generalizability.

claim: All procedures were performed in compliance with the ARVO statement for the Use of Animals in Ophthalmic and Vision Research.
source: All procedures were performed in compliance with the ARVO statement for the Use of Animals in Ophthalmic and Vision Research, and for canine studies with approval by the University of Pennsylvania Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC # 803813), and for the NHP and mouse studies with approval from the University of Pittsburgh Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC #18042326).
evidence: This is a statement of regulatory compliance.

claim: Dogs used in the study were between the age of 7 and 17 months.
source: Dogs, between the age of 7 and 17 months, were screened for neutralizing antibodies to AAV2 as previously described (Day et al., 2018).
evidence: This is experimental data about the study subjects.

claim: All dogs used in the study had AAV2 neutralizing antibody titers < 1:25.
source: All dogs had titers < 1:25.
evidence: This is experimental data about the study subjects.

claim: Marmosets, cynomolgus macaques and rhesus macaques used in the study were between 3–10 years of age.
source: Marmosets, cynomolgus macaques and rhesus macaques were between 3–10 years of age, and intravitreal injections were made with methods described previously (Dalkara et al., 2013).
evidence: This is experimental data about the study subjects.

claim: All NHPs used in the studies had anti-AAV2 neutralizing antibody titers of <1:5.
source: All NHPs used in these studies were previously screened to have anti-AAV2 neutralizing antibody titers of <1:5.
evidence: This is experimental data about the study subjects.

claim: Directed evolution was implemented to engineer new AAV vectors with the ability to bypass structural barriers and infect retinal cells following intravitreal injection in canine retinas.
source: Here, we used DE to engineer new AAV vectors with the ability to bypass structural barriers and infect retinal cells following intravitreal injection in canine retinas.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the directed evolution experiments.

claim: Canines are the main preclinical large animal model for development of retinal gene therapies.
source: Canines are the main preclinical large animal model for development of retinal gene therapies, including the landmark gene therapy clinical trials for RPE65-LCA2, due to similar ocular structure and availability of homologous mutant retinal degeneration strains (Acland et al., 2001; Beltran et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: DE was implemented similarly to the screen previously reported in primate retina.
source: DE was implemented similarly to the screen previously reported in primate retina (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 Byrne et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published literature and reference to methods.

claim: AAV2-based DE libraries were pooled and intravitreally injected into canine eyes.
source: AAV2-based DE libraries, including a ~588 peptide insertion library (which contained a random 7-mer peptide flanked by constant linker sequences LA and A, for a total of 10 amino acids inserted at VP1 position ~588) (Müller et al., 2003), an AAV2-Loopswap library (Koerber et al., 2008) and an AAV2-ErrorProne library (Koerber et al., 2006) were pooled and intravitreally injected into canine eyes (see Figure 1—figure supplement 2 for a description of each of the AAV libraries and pools used in the study).
evidence: This is experimental data supported by citations to the library sources.

claim: K916 contains a 10 amino acid insertion (PAPQDTTKKA) at position ~588.
source: The top ranked variant based on DNA recovery, K916, contains a 10 amino acid insertion (PAPQDTTKKA) at position ~588.
evidence: This is experimental data from the directed evolution screen.

claim: K912 contains a 10 amino acid insertion (LAPDSTTRSA) at position ~588.
source: The top ranked variant based on mRNA recovery, K912, contains a 10 amino acid insertion (LAPDSTTRSA) at position ~588.
evidence: This is experimental data from the directed evolution screen.

claim: K91 contains a 10 amino acid insertion (LAHQDTTKNA) at position ~588.
source: The convergent variant from the DE screen, that is, the variant that was most abundant at the end of the screen, K91, which was also overrepresented in the original library, contains a 10 amino acid insertion (LAHQDTTKNA) at position ~588.
evidence: This is experimental data from the directed evolution screen.

claim: Greatest fold increase during selection, rather than greatest frequency in the final pool, is the optimal metric for identifying top-performing variants.
source: We have previously shown that convergent variants from DE screens are not necessarily top performers (Byrne et al., 2020). That is, greatest fold increase during selection, rather than greatest frequency in the final pool, is the optimal metric for identifying top-performing variants.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and inference from the current data.

claim: A set of 17 AAV vectors were packaged individually with GFP constructs fused to unique barcodes to create the scAAVengr library.
source: A set of 17 AAV vectors were packaged individually with GFP constructs fused to unique barcodes (the scAAVengr library).
evidence: This is experimental data describing the library construction.

claim: The scAAVengr library was intravitreally injected into the eyes of 3 NHPs (2 marmosets and one cynomolgus macaque).
source: The pooled scAAVengr library was intravitreally injected into the eyes of 3 NHPs (2 marmosets and one cynomolgus macaque, Figure 1A, and see Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is experimental data describing the injection procedure.

claim: Eight weeks after intravitreal injection, samples from GFP-expressing retinas were collected.
source: Eight weeks after intravitreal injection, samples from GFP-expressing retinas were collected (Figure 1B–E).
evidence: This is experimental data describing the sample collection timeline.

claim: Clusters of all major retinal cell types were identified in marmosets and macaques.
source: Clusters of all major retinal cell types were identified in marmosets and macaques, largely in agreement with previous scRNA-seq performed in primate retina (Peng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and citation to previous work.

claim: Statistical analysis revealed a significant difference in the percent of total cells infected (p < 0.001, Friedman's test).
source: Statistical analysis revealed a significant difference in the percent of total cells infected (p < 0.001, Friedman's test, and see Supplementary files 2 and 3).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: K912 outperformed other engineered serotypes among the canine variants.
source: Of the canine variants, K912 outperformed other engineered serotypes, in agreement with the results observed in bulk analysis performed in dog retina (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the scAAVengr analysis.

claim: The convergent variant (K91) did not outperform parental serotypes.
source: The convergent variant (K91) did not outperform parental serotypes, underscoring the need for deep sequencing to determine top performing AAV variants from the DE screen.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the scAAVengr analysis.

claim: NHP26 outperformed other primate variants.
source: Of the primate variants, NHP26 outperformed other variants, infecting major retinal cell types in inner and outer retina in marmoset and cynomolgus macaque retina.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the scAAVengr analysis.

claim: Newly engineered K9 variant AAVs and NHP26 infected inner and outer retinal cells in primate retina.
source: Evaluation of AAV infectivity at cell-type resolution revealed that newly engineered K9 variant AAVs and NHP26 infected inner and outer retinal cells in primate retina (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Infectivity was most efficient in RGCs and Müller glia, particularly in the macula where the inner limiting membrane is less of an anatomical barrier.
source: Infectivity, in terms of percent cells infected, was most efficient in RGCs and Müller glia, particularly in the macula where the inner limiting membrane is less of an anatomical barrier.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and inference about anatomical barriers.

claim: Higher rates of infection and expression levels were seen in marmosets compared to the cynomolgus macaque.
source: Higher rates of infection and expression levels were seen in marmosets compared to the cynomolgus macaque.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing the two species.

claim: K912 was the overall best performing canine variant across retinal cell types.
source: These plots revealed that K912 was the overall best performing canine variant across retinal cell types, and NHP26 was the top performing primate-derived variant across cell types.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: NHP26 was the top performing primate-derived variant across cell types.
source: These plots revealed that K912 was the overall best performing canine variant across retinal cell types, and NHP26 was the top performing primate-derived variant across cell types.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: K912 was the top performer across cell types among all variants tested.
source: Of all the variants tested, K912 was the top performer across cell types.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The majority of infected cells were infected by a single variant (K912).
source: The majority of infected cells were infected by a single variant (K912), although many cells were infected by multiple serotypes (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: As many as eight serotypes infected a single cell in marmoset retina.
source: As many as eight serotypes infected a single cell in marmoset retina, while up to three serotypes infected a single cell in macaque retina.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Up to three serotypes infected a single cell in macaque retina.
source: As many as eight serotypes infected a single cell in marmoset retina, while up to three serotypes infected a single cell in macaque retina.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Pooling of AAV variants does not impede infection of other library members, either in terms of the number of cells infected or expression levels.
source: scAAVengr screening performed in HEK293 cells shows that pooling of AAV variants does not impede infection of other library members, either in terms of the number of cells infected or expression levels.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In all three conditions (AAV2 alone, with 3 additional variants, or with 16 additional variants), the number of cells infected by AAV2 and the average number of transcripts recovered from infected cells were stable.
source: In all three conditions (alone, in the presence of three additional variants, or infected in the presence of 16 additional variants), the number of cells infected by AAV2, and the average number of transcripts recovered from infected cells (averaged across all cells infected) were stable.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from in vitro experiments.

claim: Competition for receptors or the presence of additional variants in the library does not impact quantification of AAV performance.
source: Together these results indicate that competition for receptors, or the presence of additional variants in the library does not impact quantification of AAV performance.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on pooled infections.

claim: At least ~E+5 AAV variants can be quantified using the scAAVengr pipeline.
source: At least~ E + 5 AAV variants can be quantified using the scAAVengr pipeline.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: From samples containing 8000 cells, all possible barcodes were recovered from libraries with 3- and 6 bp barcodes.
source: From samples containing 8000 cells, all possible barcodes were recovered from libraries with 3- and 6 bp barcodes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from barcode recovery experiments.

claim: ~100,000 unique barcodes were recovered from 9- and 14 bp barcodes.
source: ~ 100,000 unique barcodes were recovered from 9- and 14 bp barcodes, indicating that at least E + 5 variants could be quantified using the scAAVengr pipeline.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from barcode recovery experiments.

claim: Ten weeks after injection of K912-scCAG-GFP, GFP expression was evident in retinal flatmounts and cross sections.
source: Ten weeks after injection, GFP expression was evident in retinal flatmounts and cross sections.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Confocal microscopy imaging revealed GFP expression in rods and cones, which was higher in rods than in cones.
source: Confocal microscopy imaging of PNA (which labels cone inner segments)-labeled peripheral retina, imaged at the level of the photoreceptor layer, revealed GFP expression in rods and cones, which was higher in rods than in cones, in agreement with scAAVengr heat maps.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from confocal imaging.

claim: Cross sections showed strong expression in RGCs and Müller glia, which was more efficient than in outer retina, particularly in the macula.
source: Cross sections showed strong expression in RGCs and Müller glia, which was more efficient than in outer retina, particularly in the macula, also in agreement with scAAVengr heat maps.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from histological analysis.

claim: RT-PCR shows Cas9 expression in macula of the cynomolgus macaque retina injected with K912-saCas9-gRNA-RHO but not in a control uninjected eye.
source: RT-PCR shows Cas9 expression in macula of the cynomolgus macaque retina injected with K912-saCas9-gRNA-RHO but not in a control uninjected eye.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Deep sequencing revealed that 1.8% of reads mapping to the targeted site showed editing events in the cynomolgus macaque.
source: We then used deep sequencing to quantify editing from retinal punches containing all cell types, which revealed that 1.8% of reads mapping to the targeted site showed editing events in the cynomolgus macaque and 1.7% editing in the rhesus macaque (Figure 6I and J), similar to the percent total of K912- GFP infected cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from deep sequencing analysis.

claim: 1.7% of reads showed editing in the rhesus macaque.
source: We then used deep sequencing to quantify editing from retinal punches containing all cell types, which revealed that 1.8% of reads mapping to the targeted site showed editing events in the cynomolgus macaque and 1.7% editing in the rhesus macaque (Figure 6I and J), similar to the percent total of K912- GFP infected cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from deep sequencing analysis.

claim: The editing efficiency was similar to the percent total of K912-GFP infected cells.
source: We then used deep sequencing to quantify editing from retinal punches containing all cell types, which revealed that 1.8% of reads mapping to the targeted site showed editing events in the cynomolgus macaque and 1.7% editing in the rhesus macaque (Figure 6I and J), similar to the percent total of K912- GFP infected cells.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of editing data with infection data.

claim: Individual reads revealed deletions, insertions and base substitutions in the cynomolgus macaque and rhesus macaque following injection with K912-saCas9-gRNA-RHO.
source: Individual reads revealed deletions, insertions and base substitutions in the cynomolgus macaque and rhesus macaque following injection with K912-saCas9-gRNA-RHO.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from sequencing analysis.

claim: AAV8, AAV8-2YF, AAV9, AAV9-2YF, and AAVrh.10 infected brain, heart, and liver following neonatal systemic injections.
source: Heat maps of these metrics revealed that variants AAV8, AAV8-2YF, AAV9, AAV9-2YF, and AAVrh.10 infected brain, heart, and liver following neonatal systemic injections.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: AAV1 and AAV5 also infected liver cells.
source: AAV1 and AAV5 also infected liver cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: The tropism results are in agreement with previously published data on these AAV serotypes.
source: These results are in agreement with previously published data on the tropism of these AAV serotypes (Duan, 2016; Foust et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2005; Yang et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2011; Zincarelli et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: SCH/NHP26 infected brain, heart and liver.
source: SCH/NHP26, a variant created through DE in primate with a backbone partially based on AAV9, also infected brain, heart and liver.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: AAV2-based retinal DE variants, including K912 and NHP9, did not efficiently infect organs outside of the eye.
source: In contrast, AAV2-based retinal DE variants, including K912 and NHP9, did not efficiently infect organs outside of the eye.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: By simultaneously quantifying cellular and viral RNA at the single-cell level, the scAAVengr method allows for efficient, direct, and head-to-head comparison of multiple vectors across all cell types in the same animals.
source: By simultaneously quantifying cellular and viral RNA at the single-cell level, this method allows for efficient, direct, and head-to-head comparison of multiple vectors across all cell types in the same animals.
evidence: This is an inference about the capabilities of the method based on its design.

claim: The overall rate of infection achieved by K912, around 2% of total retinal cells, suggests that significant improvements in AAV transduction must be achieved for maximal therapeutic benefit via intravitreal injections.
source: The overall rate of infection achieved by K912, around 2% of total retinal cells, suggests that significant improvements in AAV transduction must be achieved for maximal therapeutic benefit to be achieved via intravitreal injections.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on infection rates.

claim: It remains to be seen whether barriers to retinal penetration by AAV vectors from intravitreal injection can be overcome by modification of the AAV capsid alone.
source: It remains to be seen whether barriers to retinal penetration by AAV vectors from intravitreal injection can be overcome by modification of the AAV capsid alone, or whether alternative methods for vector delivery are required.
evidence: This is speculation about future research directions.

claim: Variants including K912 and NHP9, which performed well in primate retina, did not infect mouse brain, liver and heart.
source: Variants including K912 and NHP9, which performed well in primate retina, did not infect mouse brain, liver and heart, which indicates that the mutations which confer increased ability to cross structural barriers in the retina are not sufficient for infection from systemic injection in neonatal mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mouse systemic injection experiments.

claim: The mutations which confer increased ability to cross structural barriers in the retina are not sufficient for infection from systemic injection in neonatal mice.
source: Variants including K912 and NHP9, which performed well in primate retina, did not infect mouse brain, liver and heart, which indicates that the mutations which confer increased ability to cross structural barriers in the retina are not sufficient for infection from systemic injection in neonatal mice.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data comparing retinal and systemic infection.

claim: Libraries containing at least E+5 variants can be evaluated from a single sample containing 8000 cells.
source: Additional work is required to determine the maximum number of pooled AAV variants that can be screened simultaneously, though our results indicate that libraries containing at least E + 5 variants can be evaluated from a single sample containing 8000 cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from barcode recovery experiments.

claim: Multiple AAV serotypes do infect individual cells.
source: Quantification revealed that multiple AAV serotypes do infect individual cells, suggesting that competition between variants does not inhibit infection.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Competition between variants does not inhibit infection.
source: Quantification revealed that multiple AAV serotypes do infect individual cells, suggesting that competition between variants does not inhibit infection.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of multiple infections per cell.

claim: Analysis of in vitro infection of AAV variants in HEK293 cells suggests that competition between variants infecting the same cells does not significantly affect the number of infected cells or the level of transgene expression in infected cells.
source: Analysis of in vitro infection of AAV variants in HEK293 cells also suggests that competition between variants infecting the same cells does not significantly affect the number of infected cells or the level of transgene expression in infected cells, validating infectivity data from pooled AAV variants.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from in vitro experiments.

claim: Marmoset eyes were more easily infected than cynomolgus macaques, with greater percentages of cells infected and more infection events per cell.
source: Marmoset eyes, which are significantly smaller than human and macaque eyes, were more easily infected than cynomolgus macaques, with greater percentages of cells infected and more infection events per cell.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing the two species.

claim: Marmoset eyes may represent a less challenging target for AAV transduction than cynomolgus macaques due to more efficient diffusion of viral particles in smaller eyes, a less rigid vitreous consistency, or immunological factors.
source: Marmoset eyes may represent a less challenging target for AAV transduction than cynomolgus macaques due to more efficient diffusion of viral particles in smaller eyes, a less rigid vitreous consistency, or immunological factors.
evidence: This is speculation about the reasons for observed differences between species.

claim: Large primates may be of more use for accurate prediction of performance of gene delivery efficiencies in humans.
source: This suggests that large primates may be of more use for accurate prediction of performance of gene delivery efficiencies in humans, particularly in the retina, but potentially in other targets as well, such as infection of organs from systemic injections, where diffusion rates and structural barriers may differ between marmosets and macaques.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observed differences between marmosets and macaques.

claim: The rate of Cas9 editing in macaques was similar to the total percent of cells infected by K912.
source: The rate of Cas9 editing in macaques was similar to the total percent of cells infected by K912, indicating that editing was efficient in infected cells.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of editing and infection data.

claim: Similar rates of infection and genome editing indicate that scRNA-seq can accurately estimate the efficiency of viral gene delivery.
source: Importantly, similar rates of infection and genome editing indicate that scRNA-seq can accurately estimate the efficiency of viral gene delivery.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison of infection and editing rates.

claim: The scAAVengr workflow is applicable to any tissue for which cell type marker genes are available.
source: Data from primate retina and mouse brain, heart, and liver validate that the scAAVengr workflow is applicable to any tissue for which cell type marker genes are available, and provides a rapid, quantitative method by which AAV vectors can be rapidly evaluated for their clinical potential.
evidence: This is an inference about the generalizability of the method based on experimental validation in multiple tissues.

claim: The scAAVengr pipeline provides a rapid, quantitative method by which AAV vectors can be rapidly evaluated for their clinical potential.
source: Data from primate retina and mouse brain, heart, and liver validate that the scAAVengr workflow is applicable to any tissue for which cell type marker genes are available, and provides a rapid, quantitative method by which AAV vectors can be rapidly evaluated for their clinical potential.
evidence: This is an inference about the utility of the method based on its demonstrated capabilities.

claim: The quantitative nature and single-cell resolution provided by the scAAVengr pipeline enables identification and development of optimal AAV vectors for clinical translation.
source: The quantitative nature and single-cell resolution provided by the scAAVengr pipeline therefore enables identification and development of optimal AAV vectors for clinical translation.
evidence: This is an inference about the impact of the method based on its capabilities.

claim: Deep sequencing revealed ~4.8E+6 variants in the AAV2-7mer library.
source: Deep sequencing revealed ~4.8E + 6 variants in the AAV2-7mer library, which converged to ~7.1E + 4 variants in the final round of selection.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The AAV2-7mer library converged to ~7.1E+4 variants in the final round of selection.
source: Deep sequencing revealed ~4.8E + 6 variants in the AAV2-7mer library, which converged to ~7.1E + 4 variants in the final round of selection.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.
